gm.title: Statistics
lines: Speed · walk 30 ft., fly 60 ft., swim 90 ft.

gm.title: Description
lines: An orichalcum wheel with blades that races through the Ancients’ ruins to drive off intruders.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 16. Stealth 13. Resistant to acid, fire, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. Immune to poison and psychic damage, exhaustion, Blinded, Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, and Poisoned. Keensense 120 ft. Understands the languages of the Ancients and Machine Speech and has no speech.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: STR +7 · DEX +3 · CON +4 · INT -3 · WIS +6 · CHA -3

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Construct Nature. The guardian needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
Construct Resilience. The guardian ignores poison and psychic damage, exhaustion, and the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, and Poisoned conditions.
Wheelie Maneuverable. Moving out of an enemy’s reach provokes no opportunity attacks. The guardian can fit through spaces large enough for a Small or Medium creature without squeezing.
Overdrive (46 HP or fewer). Once it hits this threshold, the guardian gains advantage on melee weapon attacks and its attackers gain advantage against it. This lasts until it has more than 51 HP.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make four Whirling Blade attacks or two Flame Jet attacks.
Whirling Blade. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (1d12 + 4) slashing damage.
Flame Jet. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 21 (4d8 + 3) fire damage.
Acid Spray (Recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 30-ft. cone make a DC 15 Dexterity save against 31 (7d8) acid damage, taking half on a success.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Stunning Jolt. When a visible creature within 5 ft. hits the guardian with a melee attack, force it to make a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure the attacker is Stunned through the end of its next turn. Each time it takes damage while Stunned this way, it can repeat the save and end the effect on a success.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: A village may offer weary travelers a bed for the night. The three nights of the full moon bring a change most Quevari forget afterward.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any land. Solitary, pair, family of 2–5, or village of 20–40 plus as many noncombatants and a 3rd-level adept. Usually lawful good outside the bloodmoon and always lawful evil during it. Standard treasure. Speaks Quevari and usually one or two additional languages.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Pacifistic form. Initiative +4, touch and flat-footed AC 10. Base attack and grapple +0. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +1, Ref +2, Will +0.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Climb +14, Hide +10, Listen +8, Move Silently +10. Improved Initiative. During the bloodmoon also use Blind-Fight and Weapon Finesse with familiar melee weapons.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack in pacifistic form. Unarmed strike +0 melee (1d3 nonlethal) before the −2 morale penalty that applies to all attack rolls in this form. The Quevari fights only to defend itself.
Attack or full attack during the bloodmoon. Sickle +2 melee (1d6) or sling +5 ranged (1d4).

gm.title: Bloodmoon (Ex)
lines: On the three nights of the full moon, set Dex to 16 and Ref to +5. Use the bracketed printed AC 15, touch 13, flat-footed 12. Witnesses to the change may require a DC 15 Ravenloft Horror save. Unfamiliar melee weapons such as polearms and warhammers do not benefit from Weapon Finesse.

gm.title: Horror save
lines: Use Will against DC 15 with applicable modifiers. Failure by 1–5 gives a minor Horror effect, 6–10 a moderate one, and 11 or more a major one. Roll 1d4 on the corresponding Horror table. Failure by 16 or more also calls for an immediate DC 10 Madness save. See Ravenloft Player’s Handbook, pp. 77–83.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The Bloodmoon prose says natural armor increases by +3. The printed bracketed stat line shows +2 natural armor. This profile uses the bracketed total and derived printed ACs.

gm.title: Description
lines: An oak with a face in its bark can spy through the surrounding grove. It drags prey toward its trunk with roots that reach far beyond its branches.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any forest. Solitary or pair. Usually neutral. Standard treasure. Speaks Sylvan and may know other languages. Advancement 9–16 HD (Huge), 17–21 HD (Gargantuan).

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative −2. AC components −2 size, −2 Dex, and +13 natural. Touch 6, flat-footed 21. Base attack +6, grapple +17. Space 10 ft., reach 5 ft. or up to 90 ft. with roots. Fort +11, Ref +0, Will +4.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Plant traits, DR 10/bludgeoning or slashing, electricity resistance 20, and fire resistance 20. Camouflage (Ex). Spot, Survival, or Knowledge (plants or herbs) DC 16 to identify it before it attacks. The stat line lists blindsight 120 ft. The dedicated trait gives 60 ft. for sensing corporeal objects and creatures, in addition to normal sight.
A distressed quickwood can drum loudly enough to be heard a mile or farther.

gm.title: Skills
lines: Hide −8, Intimidate +10, Listen +12, Sense Motive +11, Spot +12, Survival +12. Add +18 racial to Hide in a forest.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +17 melee (1d6 + 11). Full attack. Eight slams +17, each for 1d6 + 11. It can attack with one root per HD. Roots extend 30 ft. each round, to a maximum of 90 ft. Each root is Medium, AC 15, with 8 HP tracked separately. It withdraws every root when half are severed.
Improved Grab and Constrict (Ex). A root slam hit allows a grapple. A successful grapple check deals 1d6 + 11 constriction damage to a Medium or smaller foe. Pull grappled foes 30 ft. per round toward the trunk. It can bite an adjacent grappled target once each round at +10 melee (1d4 + 5).
Animate Trees (Sp, at will). Control up to four normal oaks within 180 ft. Each spends a full round uprooting itself, then moves at speed 10 ft. and fights as a 3.5 treant. A tree stops moving if the quickwood is incapacitated or leaves range. As a standard action it can scry through oaks out to 1 mile. Otherwise use liveoak at caster level 12th.
Channel Fear (Su). As a free action when directly targeted by a spell, the quickwood can force all creatures within 45 ft. to make a DC 15 Ravenloft Fear save or become panicked. The spell is lost if its caster fails this save. It resolves normally if the caster succeeds or is outside the radius.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed blindsight distances conflict. Use the dedicated trait's 60-ft. range for corporeal detection. Printed hit points and grapple bonus are retained.

gm.title: Description
lines: The ghost of a cleric or paladin keeps vigil over the spot where its quest failed. Its light can blind a traveler before they see the figure inside.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +6. AC +2 Dex, +3 deflection. Touch AC 15, flat-footed AC 13. Printed base attack +6, grapple +6. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +13.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +6 melee (1d6). Full attack. Two slams +6 melee (1d6 each).
Blinding Pulse (Su). Once per minute, use a gaze attack. A failed DC 18 Fortitude save deals 1d10 damage and permanently blinds as the blindness spell at caster level 10. The victim’s corneas bear skull-shaped scars that add 1 to Outcast Rating when visible.
Frightful Moan (Su). As a standard action, force living creatures within 30 ft. to make a DC 18 Fear save. Evil creatures take a −5 morale penalty. A success grants immunity to this spirit’s moan for one day.
Sunbeam (Su). Three times per day, use sunbeam at caster level 10.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Incorporeal and undead traits, +4 turn resistance.
Radiant Aura (Su). The spirit sheds light as bright as daylight. Its continuous 30-ft. gaze blinds for 1d4 rounds on a failed DC 18 Fortitude save. It cannot suppress the aura.
Rejuvenation (Su). If destroyed, it reforms in 2d4 days. Completing its unfinished quest lays it to rest permanently.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Diplomacy +18, Knowledge (religion) +20, Listen +17, Search +20, Sense Motive +18, Spot +17. Alertness, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Toughness.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land or underground, within 1 mile of the site of its death. Solitary, always lawful evil, no treasure. Advances to 11–20 HD (Medium). Speaks languages it knew in life. It may let sympathetic travelers pass and refuses to speak to evil creatures.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Blinding Pulse gives no separate range. Use the standard 30-ft. gaze range.
The text both says it immediately attacks disrespectful intruders and describes its intended victims as evil. Its continuous gaze cannot be suppressed.

gm.title: Actions reference
lines: Bladed Chain · Melee attack · +5 to hit · 1d6 + 3 slashing damage · reach 10 ft.
Spew Flame (Recharge 4–6) · DC 13 Dexterity save · 2d8 fire damage · 15-foot cone · Half damage on a successful save

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Skills Deception +10, Insight +8 Damage Vulnerabilities piercing from magic weapons wielded by good creatures Damage Immunities bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks Senses darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 13 Languages Common, Infernal

gm.title: Traits
lines: Limited Magic Immunity. The rakshasa can’t be affected or detected by spells of 6th level or lower unless it wishes to be. It has advantage on saving throws against all other spells and magical effects. Innate Spellcasting. The rakshasa’s innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 18, +10 to hit with spell attacks). The rakshasa can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components: At will: detect thoughts, disguise self, mage hand, minor illusion 3/day each: charm person, detect magic, invisibility, major image, suggestion 1/day each: dominate person, fly, plane shift, true seeing

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The rakshasa makes two claw attacks. Claw. Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) slashing damage, and the target is cursed if it is a creature. The magical curse takes effect whenever the target takes a short or long rest, filling the target’s thoughts with horrible images and dreams. The cursed target gains no benefit from finishing a short or long rest. The curse lasts until it is lifted by a remove curse spell or similar magic.

lines: Speed · 16 in either form. Rough or broken ground does not slow the servant.

gm.title: Description
lines: A shaggy mountain ram with oversized horns. Its upright form keeps the horns, hooves and coat.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Magic resistance 30%. Exceptional intelligence 15–16. Fanatic morale 17–18.

gm.title: Traits
lines: The ram switches to humanoid form to fight unless its bearer directs otherwise. In that form it can use armor supplied by its bearer and absorb it when changing back. Both forms are immune to blunt weapons, magical or otherwise.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Head-butt, ram form. One strike for 1d8 damage, inferred from the stated double-damage running head-butt of 2d8.
Maces, humanoid form. The ram produces a double-headed mace in each hand and makes four attacks for 2d4 damage each. It reabsorbs the weapons on changing back.

gm.title: Bearer benefits
lines: The Baron of Sedhuen gains immunity to blunt weapons while in contact with the ram or carrying the coat of arms with the inactive servant.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The table lists four 2d4 attacks for the humanoid mace routine. The natural-form prose gives a charging head-butt for 2d8 and calls it double damage.

gm.title: Description
lines: A wilderness archer who can scout through an arrow fired from a Red-Feather Bow.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Studded leather. Athletics +3, Stealth +7, Survival +5. Passive Perception 13. Speaks Birdfolk and Mapach. Understands Auran.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Talons. The ranger has advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to climb surfaces their talons can grip.
Aerial Defense. Attack rolls against the ranger have disadvantage while the ranger falls, glides, or jumps.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Red-Feather Bow attacks.
Red-Feather Bow. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage.
Dagger. Weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
Talons. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines:
Arrow Sight (3/day). When the ranger fires their Red-Feather Bow, see for 1 minute from the spot where that arrow lands. If it hits a creature, see through that creature's eyes instead.
Hunter (3/day). The ranger's next shortbow or longbow attack deals an extra 1d10 damage.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Glide. After falling at least 10 ft., the ranger can spend a reaction to glide up to their speed in one direction while descending. They land in a free space at the end and take no fall damage. They need to be free of heavy objects, heavy weapons, and shields to glide. They can drop anything held as part of the same reaction.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines: The ranger casts as a 3rd-level Wisdom spellcaster (save DC 13, +5 to spell attacks). 1st level (3 slots) Cure Wounds, Fog Cloud, Hunter's Mark, Protection from Evil and Good.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Appendix B, p. 205. Ranger background, p. 203. Red-Feather Bow, Appendix D, p. 214.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed Red-Feather Bow lists 6 average damage and a roll of 1d6 + 4. Those values differ. The Dagger lists a 20/60 ft. range alongside its melee label. Use the listed range when it is thrown.

gm.title: Description
lines: An exiled Chultan paladin and former warlord who joined the yuan-ti in Omu. He hopes to free Dendar the Night Serpent, but the Soulmonger’s death curse is consuming him.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Special Equipment. Ras Nsi wears Bracers of Defense, wields a Flame Tongue Longsword, and carries the Sending Stone paired with Salida’s.
Shapechanger. As an action, he can become a Medium snake or return to yuan-ti form. His statistics stay the same, his equipment keeps its form, and he does not revert when he dies.
Magic Resistance. He has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks, using Constrict at most once.
Bite (snake form only). Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing and 7 (2d6) poison damage.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage and grapples the target (escape DC 14). The target is restrained while grappled this way. Ras Nsi can constrict only one target at a time.
Flame Tongue Longsword (yuan-ti form only). Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) with two hands, plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
Charisma, spell save DC 16. These spells require no material components.
At will: Animal Friendship (snakes only).
3/day: Suggestion.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
11th-level wizard. Intelligence, spell save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks.
Cantrips (at will): Chill Touch, Fire Bolt, Mage Hand, Mending, Poison Spray.
1st level (4 slots): Expeditious Retreat, False Life, Magic Missile, Shield.
2nd level (3 slots): Blindness/Deafness, Hold Person, Misty Step.
3rd level (3 slots): Animate Dead, Counterspell, Fireball.
4th level (3 slots): Blight, Polymorph.
5th level (2 slots): Contact Other Plane, Geas.
6th level (1 slot): Create Undead.

gm.title: Death curse
lines: The printed unweakened average is 127 HP. Begin the adventure with Ras Nsi’s maximum reduced to 107 HP. Subtract 1 more from that maximum for each day that passes.

gm.title: Fane of the Night Serpent
lines: Ras Nsi can enter any of the five disks in areas 8–12 and continue moving from any other disk in the temple. In his quarters (area 12), he can use a bonus action to say “Ssilum” and animate five shields. They initially raise his AC by 10. When they turn a hit into a miss, one drops and the bonus falls by 2. Only Ras Nsi can activate them, and their effect stays in his quarters. Once all five drop, he needs a long rest before using them again. Sekelok is his bodyguard. Acererak promised to help him free Dendar in exchange for protecting the tomb. If the party can show that stopping the death curse would help him, Ras Nsi may let them proceed.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 230. Death curse context, pp. 229–230. Fane teleporters and flying shields, pp. 114 and 121.

gm.title: Description
lines: A tusked squirrel-like celestial that once carried messages between the gods and now uses secrets to start arguments.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Perception 12, Stealth 16. Resistant to radiant damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks. Darkvision 60 ft. Languages Celestial and Common, telepathy 100 ft.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str -3, Dex +4, Con +1, Int +3, Wis +2, Cha +6

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Celestial Resilience. Resistant to radiant damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
Magic Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Gore or Annoying Chitter attacks. The ratatosk can replace one with Spellcasting or Divisive Chatter if available.
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.
Annoying Chitter. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit 14 (3d6 + 4) psychic damage.
Divisive Chatter (recharge 5–6). Choose up to four creatures the ratatosk can see within 30 ft. Each makes a DC 14 Charisma save. On a failure, it spends its action each turn arguing with an ally, complaining about an ally, or otherwise showing displeasure toward an ally over a trivial matter for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines: Charisma, save DC 14, no material or somatic components. At will: Animal Messenger, Message. Three times per day each: Sending, Suggestion.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Desperate Lies. When a visible creature targets the ratatosk with an attack, the ratatosk points to another creature within 5 ft. of itself and lies. The attacker must pass a DC 14 Wisdom save or attack the creature it pointed to instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: An oversized black bird with a taste for bright trinkets. A ravenkin shares magic with ordinary ravens and may trade information with someone it trusts.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any temperate land. Solitary, murder of 5–20, or community of 100–200 plus 10% noncombatants and 200–300 ravens. Always good, usually neutral good. Standard treasure. Advances by character class, level adjustment +2. Speaks Ravenkin and usually at least one domain language.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +8. AC +1 size and +4 Dex. Touch 15, flat-footed 11. Base attack +2, grapple +1 as printed. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +1, Ref +7, Will +5.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Appraise +12, Concentration +7, Gather Information +10, Knowledge (arcana) +12, Listen +10, Sense Motive +10, Spot +12. +8 racial bonus on Appraise, Gather Information, Survival, and Spot. Improved Critical (bite), Improved Initiative, Flyby Attack, Still Spell, and Weapon Finesse. All listed except Flyby Attack are bonus feats.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Ravenlink (Su). Can share spells with an ordinary raven within 5 ft. At 3 HD or more, can deliver touch spells through an ordinary raven within 60 ft. At 13 HD or more, it can touch an ordinary raven once per day to scry through it as a spellcaster would through a familiar.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Bite +7 melee (1d3 − 1), threat range 19–20.
Eye Peck (Ex). A confirmed critical hit with the bite removes one eye. A target left with only one eye takes a −2 competence penalty to Dexterity-modified rolls. A creature that loses all eyes is blinded. Only regenerate or heal can reverse this blindness.
Spells. Casts as a 1st-level sorcerer. Choose the spells when preparing the encounter, since the printing does not give a spells-known list. It uses Still Spell to cast while flying.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed grapple modifier is +1, although base attack +2, Strength 9 and Small size ordinarily total −3. The encounter retains the printed number.

gm.title: Description
lines: This low-slung plains hunter runs beneath its prey and cuts it with the raised spines along its back.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +3. AC components +1 size, +3 Dex, +5 natural. Touch 14, flat-footed 16. Base attack +1, grapple −2. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +4, Ref +6, Will +1.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Rake +3 melee for 1d8 + 1 and wounding.
Full attack. Use the same rake, or make two claws at −2 melee for 1d4 each and a bite at −2 melee for 1d6 + 1.
Rake on a charge. Target a creature from Medium through Huge (long). Add the usual +2 charge bonus to the printed attack. The razorback can pass through the target’s square without provoking from that movement and can continue up to a total of double its speed.
Wounding (Ex). Each spine wound deals 1 HP of bleeding damage per round. Bleeding from multiple wounds stacks. A DC 15 Heal check or any healing magic stops it. Creatures immune to critical hits are immune to this bleeding.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Scent. Packs usually each choose a target, but they may charge one large foe in succession and follow it while it bleeds.

gm.title: Skills
lines: Hide +8, Listen +5, Move Silently +7, Spot +5. Racial bonuses are +4 to Hide and Move Silently. The Hide racial bonus increases to +8 in tall grass or heavy undergrowth.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Temperate or warm plains. Solitary, pair, or pack of 2–8. Always neutral. No treasure. Advancement 3–5 HD Small, then 6–8 HD Medium.

gm.title: Description
lines: A humanoid reanimator depicted in the publisher preview with copper goggles and a leather harness.

gm.title: Source coverage
lines: The Fantasy Grounds preview shows the core defenses and movement. The actions are outside the visible preview.

gm.title: Description
lines: A fishlike raider uses its blade-edged scales to cut creatures it gets hold of. In groups, reavers strike boats or houses after dark.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Temperate or warm aquatic environments, notably the Sea of Sorrows. Solitary or school of 10–15. Always chaotic evil. Standard treasure. Advances by character class, level adjustment +3. Communicates with hisses and ultrasonic calls.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +0. AC +6 natural. Touch 10, flat-footed 16. Base attack +4, grapple +8. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +2, Ref +4, Will +6.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Hide +6, Listen +5, Move Silently +4, Profession (hunter) +4, Spot +5, Survival +4. Add a +4 racial bonus to each of those underwater. Cleave and Power Attack.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious (Ex). It breathes air and water. After 1 hour per point of Constitution out of water, apply the drowning rules.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +8 melee (1d6 + 4).
Full attack. Two claws +8 melee (1d6 + 4 each) and bite +3 melee (1d4 + 2).
Improved Grab (Ex). A single claw hit can start a grapple against a target up to Small. Both claws must hit the same target to grab an opponent up to Medium.
Cutting Scales (Ex). A creature grappling the reaver takes 1d6 slashing damage automatically, regardless of which creature began the grapple.

gm.title: Description
lines: A red-haired stranger lures prey into a webbed hideout, then drops the disguise and reveals a red-and-black spider.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any temperate or cold land. Solitary or pair. Usually neutral evil. Standard treasure. Advancement 7–9 HD (Medium) or 10–12 HD (Large). No level adjustment. Speaks its homeland’s domain languages.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +6 in either form. Base attack +4, grapple +6. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +7, Ref +7, Will +6 in both forms.

gm.title: Humanoid form
lines: AC 12 (+2 Dex), touch 12, flat-footed 10. Speed 30 ft. Attack or full attack is one unarmed strike +6 melee (1d3 + 2).

gm.title: Spider form
lines: AC 18 (+2 Dex, +6 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 16. Speed 30 ft., climb 20 ft. Attack or full attack is one bite +6 melee (1d4 + 2 plus poison). The widow’s special attacks are limited to this form.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +14, Climb +10, Diplomacy +12, Listen +3, Sense Motive +10 in either form. Humanoid Jump +4 and Spot +3. Spider Hide +6, Jump +10, Move Silently +6, and Spot +11. The listed skill totals include racial bonuses to Bluff, Diplomacy, and Sense Motive and, in spider form, to Jump and Spot. The widow also gains a +8 competence bonus to Hide and Move Silently around its webs. Alertness, Improved Initiative (bonus), Skill Focus (Bluff).

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Darkvision 60 ft.
Alternate Form (Su). As a standard action, assume its one specific humanoid form as if using polymorph. Gear stays as it is. Death restores spider form. A widow can switch forms while maintaining a pin.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Use the attack listed for the current form.
Poison (Ex). On a bite hit, Fortitude DC 15. Initial damage 1d6 Strength, secondary damage 2d6 Strength.
Fluid Drain (Ex). In spider form, pin a living creature using a successful grapple check to drain 1d4 Constitution per round the pin holds. Each Constitution point consumed sustains the widow for a day.
Web (Ex). Use the 3.5 Medium monstrous spider rules. Throw a web up to eight times per day as a net-like ranged touch attack (10-ft. range increment, 50-ft. maximum) against a target up to Large. A trapped creature can spend a standard action to attempt DC 12 Escape Artist or DC 16 Strength. A Medium web has 6 HP. A widow that wins an opposed Strength check against a webbed victim can pull it 10 ft. closer as a standard action.
Infest (Ex). A widow can implant 2d4 eggs in a paralyzed mate once a year and wrap the target in webbing. Remove the eggs before they hatch in 1d6 days. After hatching each young deals 1 HP of damage to the host per day. Immature young use monstrous spider statistics until they mature at one year.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The habitat and combat prose describe paralysis during infestation, but the Poison entry specifies Strength damage and supplies no separate paralysis rules.

gm.title: Description
lines: A Large aberration with challenge rating 10. Named abilities include Reduced Threat, Amphibious, Mucous Cloud.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Saving Throws Con +4, Int +6, Wis +4 Skills History +10, Perception +8 Senses darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 20 Languages Deep Speech, telepathy 120 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious. The aboleth can breathe air and water. Mucous Cloud. While underwater, the aboleth is surrounded by transformative mucus. A creature that touches the aboleth or that hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature is diseased for 1d4 hours. The diseased creature can breathe only underwater. Probing Telepathy. If a creature communicates telepathically with the aboleth, the aboleth learns the creature’s greatest desires if the aboleth can see the creature.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The aboleth makes three tentacle attacks. Tentacle. Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or become diseased. The disease has no effect for 1 minute and can be removed by any magic that cures disease. After 1 minute, the diseased creature’s skin becomes translucent and slimy, the creature can’t regain hit points unless it is underwater, and the disease can be removed only by heal or another disease-curing spell of 6th level or higher. When the creature is outside a body of water, it takes 6 (1d12) acid damage every 10 minutes unless moisture is applied to the skin before 10 minutes have passed. Tail. Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft. one target. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. Enslave (3/Day). The aboleth targets one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be magically charmed by the aboleth until the aboleth dies or until it is on a different plane of existence from the target. The charmed target is under the aboleth’s control and can’t take reactions, and the aboleth and the target can communicate telepathically with each other over any distance. Whenever the charmed target takes damage, the target can repeat the saving throw. On a success, the effect ends. No more than once every 24 hours, the target can also repeat the saving throw when it is at least 1 mile away from the aboleth.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines: The aboleth can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature’s turn. The aboleth regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn. Detect. The aboleth makes a Wisdom (Perception) check. Tail Swipe. The aboleth makes one tail attack. Psychic Drain (Costs 2 Actions). One creature charmed by the aboleth takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage, and the aboleth regains hit points equal to the damage the creature takes.

lines: Petrifying Gaze. If a creature starts its turn within 30 feet of the basilisk and the two of them can see each other, the basilisk can force the creature to make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw if the basilisk isn’t incapacitated. On a failed save, the creature magically begins to turn to stone and is restrained. It must repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn. On a success, the effect ends. On a failure, the creature is petrified until freed by the greater restoration spell or other magic. A creature that isn’t surprised can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If it does so, it can’t see the basilisk until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If it looks at the basilisk in the meantime, it must immediately make the save. If the basilisk sees its reflection within 30 feet of it in bright light, it mistakes itself for a rival and targets itself with its gaze.

While swallowed, the target is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the behir, and it takes 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each of the behir’s turns. A behir can have only one creature swallowed at a time. If the behir takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from the swallowed creature, the behir must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate the creature, which falls prone in a space within 10 feet of the behir. If the behir dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 15 feet of movement, exiting prone.

The golem’s creator, if within 60 feet of the berserk golem, can try to calm it by speaking firmly and persuasively. The golem must be able to hear its creator, who must take an action to make a DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check. If the check succeeds, the golem ceases being berserk. gm.title: Description
lines: A jewel-bright cloaker waits on furniture for a suitable host. It feeds by mending wounds, and its glow draws unwanted eyes.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +7. AC components −1 size, +3 Dex, +5 natural. Touch AC 12, flat-footed AC 14. Base attack +4. Space 10 ft., reach 10 ft. Fort +9, Ref +5, Will +7. Standard treasure.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Attach +8 melee touch (no damage).
Full attack. Attach +8 melee touch (no damage) and bite +3 melee (1d4 + 2), as printed.
Color Spray (Su). Release a burst that works like color spray from a 6th-level sorcerer. DC 16 Will negates.
Attach (Su). If the spray stuns or knocks out a human-shaped living creature at least one size smaller, attempt a touch attack to make it a host.
Hit Point Drain (Su). As a free action each round, heal up to 5 HP of damage to either the cloaker or its host. For every 2 HP it heals on the host, it feeds on 1 HP of that damage. When it heals itself from its host, the host takes 2 damage for each HP the cloaker regains. It cannot heal damage it inflicted. If it fails to feed on at least 1 HP of damage in a day, it takes 1 damage.

gm.title: Host and vulnerabilities
lines: It detaches if the host dies, if either the host or the cloaker receives magical healing, or if it goes four days without feeding. A DC 15 Strength check can tear it free. Both make DC 14 Fortitude saves or die, and a surviving host is stunned for 1d8 minutes. The cloaker loses 1 HD per week without a host and recovers 1 HD per day of feeding on a new host. Magical darkness deals 1 damage per round to the cloaker. Healing magic applied to the cloaker deals the amount that would be healed to both it and its host.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Hide +12, Listen +11, Move Silently +12, Spot +11. Its glow grants observers a +10 circumstance bonus to Spot it except in very bright light. Feats: Alertness, Improved Initiative.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Underground. Solitary. Usually chaotic neutral. Advancement 7–9 HD (Large), 10–18 HD (Huge).

lines:
Printed source. Cloaker, Dread, p. 51.
Damage reduction (Su). A cloaker draped around its host shares its damage reduction against physical attacks other than area attacks.
Engulf (Ex). As a standard action, the cloaker envelops a creature at least one size category smaller. Its host is engulfed automatically. Any other target requires a successful grapple check without provoking an attack of opportunity. The target is pinned. A cloaker without a host gains +4 to bite the engulfed creature.
Split damage from attacks that hit an engulfing cloaker equally between it and its victim. Area spells deal full damage to both. A shadow or undead cloaker can still strike other targets with its tail while engulfing a creature.

lines: A Void predator opens unstable rifts with its oversized claws. It looks for vulnerable worlds and may open a rift for someone whose aims it shares.

gm.title: Other statistics

lines: Str +8, Dex +3, Con +5, Int +3, Wis +7, Cha +2

lines: Aberrant Resilience. Resistance to Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned. Advantage on saves against spells or effects that change its form.

lines:

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

Destroying a tendril deals no damage to the roper, which can extrude a replacement tendril on its next turn. A tendril can also be broken if a creature takes an action and succeeds on a DC 15 Strength check against it. Spider Climb. The roper can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Description
lines: A sea spawn master uses parasitic minions to infiltrate coastal communities and draw prey into the water.

gm.title: Running the encounter
lines: A master releases 3d6 minions near the shore each night until it controls the village. Roughly one in ten reaches shore. A minion paralyzes a host, burrows into its skull, and takes control. Use the Sea Spawn Minion entry for implantation, removal, and daily effects.

gm.title: Coordinated response
lines: The master stays in shallow coastal water and maintains a telepathic link with its brood. If a minion or its host is threatened, it can call on nearby controlled hosts and minions. Use the Sea Spawn Master entry for the submerged confrontation and aquatic allies.

gm.title: Signs and escalation
lines: The minions favor children and infirm people. They abduct others and deliver them to the master. Once the village is under control, the minions drive their own hosts into the sea to feed the master. The occasional survivor matures into a new master after a year.

Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Immune to necrotic and poison damage and to Charmed, Dazed, Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, and Unconscious. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 10. Speaks the languages it knew in life.

gm.title: Description
lines: This cloaker moves like a patch of darkness, then latches onto a lone traveler’s shadow and feeds through their touch.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +7. AC components −1 size, +3 Dex, +7 natural. Touch AC 12, flat-footed AC 16. Base attack +4. Space 10 ft., reach 10 ft. (5 ft. with bite). Fort +9, Ref +5, Will +7. Standard treasure.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Tail slap +8 melee (1d6 + 5).
Full attack. Tail slap +8 melee (1d6 + 5) and bite +3 melee (1d4 + 2). It can use the tail on another target while engulfing and can use the tail while attached.
Attach (Su). On a bite that hits a human-shaped living creature at least one size smaller, attach to its shadow. It cannot bite while attached. This ends when either dies or when a daylight, sunbeam, or sunburst spell targets the cloaker. Without a host it loses 1 HD per week, recovering 1 HD per day of feeding through a new host.
Constitution Drain (Su). The cloaker feeds once per day. Its host’s contact with a living creature deals 1 point of Constitution drain to that creature 2d8 minutes later. Against an unwilling creature, the host must make a touch attack. If the host touches no living creature for 24 hours, the cloaker feeds from the host. A creature drained to Constitution 0 dies and rises as a shadow 24 hours later.
Shadow Shift (Su). The cloaker and its host gain concealment (20% miss chance) for 1d4 rounds.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Hide +12, Listen +11, Move Silently +12, Spot +11. In shadowy areas it gains a +5 racial bonus on Hide checks (total +17), and a host also gains that +5 racial bonus. A successful Move Silently check lets the cloaker gain surprise when it attacks. Feats: Alertness, Improved Initiative.

gm.title: Shared dread cloaker rules
lines:
Printed source. Cloaker, Dread, p. 51.
Damage reduction (Su). A cloaker draped around its host shares its damage reduction against physical attacks other than area attacks.
Engulf (Ex). As a standard action, the cloaker envelops a creature at least one size category smaller. Its host is engulfed automatically. Any other target requires a successful grapple check without provoking an attack of opportunity. The target is pinned. A cloaker without a host gains +4 to bite the engulfed creature.
Split damage from attacks that hit an engulfing cloaker equally between it and its victim. Area spells deal full damage to both. A shadow or undead cloaker can still strike other targets with its tail while engulfing a creature.

lines: Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks while the mastiff is in dim light or darkness.

lines:

gm.title: Description
lines: This featureless dream creature takes the shape of a dreamer’s old enemy or a lost loved one.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +5. AC 16 (+1 Dex, +5 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 15. Base attack +5, grapple +7. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +6, Ref +5, Will +6.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +7 melee (1d4+2). Full attack. Two claws +7 melee (1d4+2 each).
Lullaby (Su). As a standard action, opponents within 20 ft. must make a DC 14 Will save. Failure fatigues them for 1d4 rounds or as long as the dream spawn keeps speaking within 20 ft. of them. Maintaining the lullaby is a free action. This is a sonic, mind-affecting compulsion.
Memory Drain (Su, 1/day). A successful touch attack deals 1d4 Intelligence damage. Until the victim recovers all of those points, the dream spawn can use Alternate Form to impersonate any creature from the victim's memory.
Alternate Form (Su). Use polymorph on itself as a standard action at caster level 8. The form can last indefinitely. Returning to its own shape is a free action.
Nightmare Howl (Su). As a standard action, opponents within 60 ft. make a DC 14 Will save. Failure paralyzes the creature with fear for 1d4 rounds and heals the shadow morph for 1d4 HP per failed save. Anyone exposed is immune to that morph's howl for 1 day. All dream spawn are immune. This is a sonic, mind-affecting fear effect.

gm.title: Traits
lines: DR 10/magic. Darkvision 60 ft. It does not need to eat, drink, or breathe. Detect Thoughts (Su). In an inhabited dreamscape, it knows a creature's surface thoughts as though it had studied them for three rounds with detect thoughts, caster level 5, Will DC 14. Fear Eater (Ex). Immune to Fear, Horror, and Madness. A spell targeting it that would normally cause one of those effects heals 1 HP per spell level. When one of its actions makes a dreamer fail a Fear, Horror, or Madness save, it heals 2 HP for a minor outcome, 4 HP for a moderate outcome, or 8 HP for a major outcome.

gm.title: Dream defeat
lines: A dreamer killed by this dream spawn takes a DC 14 Ravenloft Madness save on waking (Will). For consequences and recovery, use the Ravenloft Player’s Handbook, chapter 3. A spawn that wins often returns to terrorize that dreamer again.

gm.title: Description
lines: A black garment adapts to its wearer and trades powers for experience. If starved or threatened with death, it may take the wearer into the Plane of Shadows.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Tiny item or Medium shadow creature

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Very rare, appearing 1d4. Neutral. Intelligence 11–12. No treasure or magic resistance. Immune to the Red Curse.

gm.title: Actions
lines: On the Prime Material Plane, the worn form has AC 10, 1 HD, THAC0 19, no movement or attacks, steady morale 11–12 and an XP value of 120. No magical aura betrays it. On the Plane of Shadows it becomes a humanoid with AC 2, 8 HD, THAC0 13, movement 15, champion morale 15–16 and an XP value of 5,000. It attacks twice for 2d4 each. Each hit drains 10% of the experience needed for a level and 1 point of Strength or Constitution, chosen at equal odds.

gm.title: Mask
lines: The wearer concentrates to gain immunity to mind-affecting magic, at 20 XP per use per wearer level. In the Plane of Shadows the symbiont has that immunity itself.

gm.title: Cloak
lines: Absorbs all magical HP damage from a hit that would reduce the wearer below 0 HP. Costs 10 XP per point absorbed per wearer level. In the Plane of Shadows, subtract 8 points of damage from each attack against the symbiont.

gm.title: Gloves
lines: Give the wearer the Luck Legacy for hand-related actions only, allowing a reroll of a failed save or ability check when applicable. Costs 20 XP per use per wearer level. In the Plane of Shadows, the symbiont itself has Luck.

gm.title: Boots
lines: Allow the wearer to cast dimension door for 10 XP per use per wearer level. The boots can also guide the wearer toward opportunities to earn XP at no cost, without controlling decisions. In the Plane of Shadows they cast dimension door as an 8th-level mage once per round.

gm.title: Feeding and defense
lines: Only spells and weapons of +1 or better can harm the symbiont. Any damage it suffers also harms the wearer. A lethal attempt makes it flee by plane shift with the wearer. A wearer who gains too little new XP to feed it saves vs. spell. Success makes it drain three times the missing XP before slipping away. On failure it takes the wearer to the Plane of Shadows and tries to devour them.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The encounter gives each power’s XP cost and describes the consequences of shortfalls, without prescribing a separate feeding schedule.

lines: When using the Ravenloft Fear rules, roll a Will save. Apply modifiers to saves against fear. Failure by 1–5 makes the target shaken, 6–10 frightened, and 11–15 panicked. gm.title: Hit point rule
lines: 7 + 7 × the caregiver’s level in hit points, with one d8 Hit Die per caregiver level.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A compact, fern-covered mound with two lashing vines and a woven pocket that can hold prey.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Armor class 13 + PB. Constitution save +2 + PB. Skills Athletics +3 + PB and Perception +PB. Poison damage immunity. Immune to Blinded and Poisoned. Blindsight 60 ft., blind beyond that range. Passive Perception 10 + PB.

gm.title: Caregiver scaling
lines: PB is the caregiver’s proficiency bonus.

gm.title: Traits
lines: False Appearance. A motionless mound looks like ordinary vegetation. A caregiver of Large size or smaller can take the Hide action to try to hide in its space while it remains still.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Signature Attack (Vine Lash). Melee weapon attack at +3 + PB, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1d6 + PB piercing damage.

gm.title: Ferocity actions
lines:
Level 1, Long-Range Lash (2 Ferocity). Make a signature attack at 30-ft. reach. On a hit against a Medium or smaller creature, the mound can pull it up to 10 ft.
Level 3, Verdant Roundup (5 Ferocity). Choose up to PB Large or smaller creatures within 30 ft. Each makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB. On a failure, the target is pulled up to 15 ft. toward the mound and takes PBd4 poison damage.
Level 5, Engulf (8 Ferocity). One Large or smaller creature within 5 ft. makes a Strength save against DC 10 + PB. A failure pulls it into the mound’s space, deals PBd8 poison damage and engulfs it. A success deals half damage and leaves it in place. While engulfed it moves with the mound, is Restrained, has total cover from outside effects and takes PBd8 poison damage at the start of each of the mound’s turns. It can spend an action on a Strength check against DC 10 + PB to escape into a free space of its choice within 5 ft. The mound can hold one Large creature or up to four Medium or smaller creatures.

gm.title: Mystic connection
lines: Maw of the Mound. At 9th level, a Beastheart with this companion and Mystic Connection can use a bonus action to bite an enemy with an unarmed strike. Use Strength or Dexterity to hit and for damage. A hit deals 1d6 plus the chosen modifier in piercing damage and grants temporary HP equal to the damage dealt. Uses equal PB and refresh on a long rest.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A low heap of wet leaves, roots and grabbing fronds, smaller than a full-grown shambling mound.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Poison damage immunity. Immune to Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Flanked, Frightened, Poisoned and Prone. Blindsight 60 ft., blind beyond that range. Passive Perception 10. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
False Appearance. A motionless pile passes for an ordinary heap of vegetation.
Hungry Grab. An enemy starting its turn within 5 ft. of at least three piles makes a Dexterity save or is Grappled. While grappled this way, it is Restrained and takes poison damage at the start of each of its turns equal to the number of piles within 5 ft. of it. The save and escape DC are 10 plus that number. The grapple ends if fewer than three piles remain within 5 ft.
Minion. Damage from an attack or failed saving throw drops the pile to 0 HP. It ignores other damage below 12 and dies if such an effect deals at least 12 damage.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Vine Lash (Group Attack). Melee weapon attack +6, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 4 piercing damage.

gm.title: Minion rules
lines:
Group attack. Two to five piles on the same turn can each spend an action to lash one target within reach of all of them. Make a single attack at +6 plus the number joining. A hit deals 4 piercing damage per pile. A solo pile attacks at +6. If all participants have advantage or disadvantage, so does the roll. Separate groups when cover or concealment differs. The target chooses one attacker for a response that can only affect one.
Group opportunity attack. If the target provokes from multiple piles at once, each can spend its reaction to join. Piles have no Hit Dice and cannot score critical hits.
Overkill. After a weapon attack exceeds a pile’s 12 HP, each additional 12 points of damage or part of 12 can drop another eligible pile to 0 HP. For melee, each additional pile must be within the weapon’s reach. For ranged, it must be on the line from attacker through the original target and within the weapon’s short range. This rule does not apply to opportunity attacks.

gm.title: Other statistics

gm.title: Actions

Attack or full attack. Shortbow +8 ranged (1d6) or light crossbow +8 ranged (1d8).
Cursed Arrows (Su). The shee's arrows and bolts inflict doom as the spell unless the target succeeds on a DC 14 Will save.

gm.title: Description
lines: A gaunt Unseelie spellcaster who prefers to travel as a shadow and reappears with a rapier in hand.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +2. AC 15 (+2 Dex, +3 luck), touch 15, flat-footed 13. Base attack +3, grapple +3. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +2, Ref +2, Will +5.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Rapier +6 melee (1d6).
Full attack. Three rapier strikes +6 melee (1d6 each) with Blinding Speed. A sith cannot use Blinding Speed if wielding a heavy weapon.
Fear Aura (Su). At will, opponents within 30 ft. make a DC 14 Will save or are stunned for 1 round. A successful save grants immunity to this sith's aura for 1 day.
Shadow Form (Su). As a standard action, assume the appearance of a nonmagical shadow. In this form the sith can move and perceive its surroundings, but cannot attack.

gm.title: Traits
lines: DR 5/silver. Immune to fire. Darkvision 120 ft. and low-light vision. The +3 luck bonus to AC is already included. Reroll one failed save per day. Direct sunlight deals 3 damage each round without a save. Shade reduces this to 1 damage per round.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines: Casts Necromancy spells as a 6th-level wizard. No prepared spell list is given. For a quick encounter, ray of enfeeblement, blindness/deafness, and vampiric touch are options. Spell save DC 13 + spell level.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Craft (alchemy) +10, Decipher Script +10, Gather Information +10, Hide +12, Knowledge (arcana) +10, Listen +15, Move Silently +9, Ride +8, Spellcraft +10, Spot +10, Use Magic Device +10. Scribe Scroll, Silent Spell, Still Spell. Speaks Sylvan and at least four local languages.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land in the Shadow Rift. Solitary or bevy of 3–5. Standard treasure. Always lawful evil.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The source describes Blinding Speed as three full attacks and gives a three-strike full-attack line. Use that line as the total rather than multiplying it again.
The source says ‘damage resistance 5/silver.’ This profile treats that notation as damage reduction, consistent with the other shadow fey.

gm.title: Other statistics

gm.title: Actions

Claw pass. Make two claw attacks for 1d4 each from above or behind, then fly out of reach. A flock normally concentrates these passes on one target. If both claws hit and the victim weighs less than half the skinwing’s carrying capacity, carry it aloft and deal 2d4 damage per round thereafter.

A skinwing carrying a rider cannot attack.

At the start of each of the trapped creature’s turns, it takes 7 (2d6) slashing plus 7 (2d6) poison damage. A Humanoid reduced to 0 HP by this damage is stable and Paralyzed for 12 hours or until it regains HP. Capacity one. If the creature inside deals at least 15 damage in a single turn, the skogsra makes a DC 13 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On a failure it expels the creature Prone within 5 ft. If the skogsra dies, the restraint and paralysis from the trap end, and the creature can spend 5 ft. of movement to exit Prone.

gm.title: Dread golem commands
lines: The creator can give commands from within 60 ft. if the golem can see and hear them. It follows the last command and responds to attacks against it. Some dread golems act independently.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Angelic Weapons. The solar’s weapon attacks are magical. When the solar hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 6d8 radiant damage (included in the attack). Divine Awareness. The solar knows if it hears a lie. Innate Spellcasting. The solar’s spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 25). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components: At will: detect evil and good, invisibility (self only) 3/day each: blade barrier, dispel evil and good, resurrection 1/day each: commune, control weather Magic Resistance. The solar has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The solar makes two greatsword attacks. Greatsword. Melee Weapon Attack: +15 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (4d6 + 8) slashing damage plus 27 (6d8) radiant damage. Slaying Longbow. Ranged Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) piercing damage plus 27 (6d8) radiant damage. If the target is a creature that has 100 hit points or fewer, it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or die. Flying Sword. The solar releases its greatsword to hover magically in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it. If the solar can see the sword, the solar can mentally command it as a bonus action to fly up to 50 feet and either make one attack against a target or return to the solar’s hands. If the hovering sword is targeted by any effect, the solar is considered to be holding it. The hovering sword falls if the solar dies. Healing Touch (4/Day). The solar touches another creature. The target magically regains 40 (8d8 + 4) hit points and is freed from any curse, disease, poison, blindness, or deafness.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines: The solar can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature’s turn. The solar regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn. Teleport. The solar magically teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. Searing Burst (Costs 2 Actions). The solar emits magical, divine energy. Each creature of its choice in a 10-foot radius must make a DC 23 Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) fire damage plus 14 (4d6) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Blinding Gaze (Costs 3 Actions). The solar targets one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. If the target can see it, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be blinded until magic such as the lesser restoration spell removes the blindness.

gm.title: Description
lines: One of the most powerful angels. Its greatsword can fly and fight on command. A shot from its longbow can kill outright.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Radiant. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Angelic Weapons. Its weapon attacks count as magical and deal an extra 6d8 radiant damage on a hit. The attack entries include that extra damage.
Divine Awareness. It recognizes a lie when it hears one.
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Immortal Nature. It needs no food, drink, or sleep.

gm.title: Innate spellcasting
lines:
Charisma is its spellcasting ability (save DC 25). It casts these spells without material components.
At will. Detect Evil and Good, Invisibility (self only).
3/day each. Blade Barrier, Dispel Evil and Good, Resurrection.
1/day each. Commune, Control Weather.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Greatsword attacks.
Greatsword. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 22 (4d6 + 8) slashing damage plus 27 (6d8) radiant damage.
Slaying Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +13 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 15 (2d8 + 6) piercing damage plus 27 (6d8) radiant damage. A creature hit with 100 HP or fewer makes a DC 15 Constitution save or dies.
Flying Sword. Release the greatsword into an unoccupied space within 5 ft., where it hovers by magic. The sword falls if the solar dies. Effects that target the hovering sword treat the solar as holding it.
Healing Touch (4/day). Touch another creature. It magically regains 40 (8d8 + 4) HP and loses any curse, disease, poison, blindness, or deafness.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Command Flying Sword. While the solar sees its hovering sword, it can mentally order it to fly up to 50 ft. and either make one attack or return to the solar's hands.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The solar has 3 legendary actions. It can take one option at the end of another creature's turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using them. Assuming the solar's form does not grant these actions.
Teleport. Magically teleport up to 120 ft. to a visible unoccupied space, taking worn and carried gear.
Searing Burst (2 actions). Each creature the solar chooses within 10 ft. makes a DC 23 Dexterity save against its divine magic. On a failure take 14 (4d6) fire damage plus 14 (4d6) radiant damage. On a success take half.
Blinding Gaze (3 actions). Choose a visible creature within 30 ft. that can see the solar. It makes a DC 15 Constitution save or is Blinded until magic, such as Lesser Restoration, removes the blindness.

lines: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 15 and 18. The official errata corrects the Slaying Longbow range and updates resistance and legendary action timing.

Printed source. Hag, Spectral, pp. 108–111.
Chilling Touch (Su). A target hit by the spectral hag’s incorporeal touch makes a DC 15 Fortitude save. Failure gives it 2 negative levels. The touch still deals its listed hit point damage on a successful save.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: A white hound with a broad muzzle and long, floppy ears. Its humanoid form looks much like a white-haired lupin.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Magic resistance 25%. High intelligence 13–14. Fanatic morale 17–18.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Tracking. Its sharp hearing and sense of smell detect and track enemies in either form. The humanoid can use the skills and weapons of a 6th-level ranger. The bearer supplies the gear, which the servant absorbs when changing back.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite, natural form. One bite for 2d4. In humanoid form, attack with a ranger weapon provided by its bearer.
Invisibility. Turn invisible at will in either form. Ambushes made this way gain +3 to surprise.

gm.title: Bearer benefits
lines: The King of Renardy, Duke of Ysembragne, Baron of Brégoigne, and Countess of Marmandy are known bearers. While in contact, the bearer gains the keen senses and can turn invisible three times per day. Telepathic contact or carrying the coat of arms with the inactive servant also grants the ranger bonuses against giant-class creatures.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The entry names the ranger bonus against giant-class creatures without supplying its numeric value.

lines: Targor leads the optional returning war band. He travels with three other hobgoblins and two pet wolves. A successful DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check can convince him to claim leadership instead of avenging King Grol. Resolving the encounter by combat or negotiation awards 500 XP to the party.

lines:

1st (4 slots) · Detect Magic, Heroism, Identify, Shield.
2nd (3 slots) · Alter Self, Branding Smite, See Invisibility, Warding Bond.
3rd (3 slots) · Dispel Magic, Fly, Haste, Magic Circle, Revivify.

gm.title: Description
lines: A second shadow follows its host by day. At night the outsider uses the sleeping host’s body to act on grudges that the host mistakes for dreams.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +3. AC +3 Dex, +2 deflection. Touch AC 15, flat-footed AC 12. Printed base attack +8, grapple +8. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +6, Ref +6, Will +6.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack and full attack. Use the host’s attacks.
Malevolent Possession (Su). Once a night, enter a sleeping creature on the Material Plane unless it passes a DC 20 Will save. Use magic jar at caster level 10 without a receptacle. It takes over the body and controls dreams as a 10th-level sorcerer using dream. A success grants immunity to its possession that night.
Wisdom Drain (Su). Once per night the possessed creature takes 1d4 Wisdom drain unless it passes a DC 29 Will save.
Spell-like abilities. Twice per day each: bane, charm person, command, confusion, crushing despair, mind fog, and undetectable alignment. Caster level 10, save DC 15 + spell level. Detect thoughts is listed separately without a specified frequency.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Incorporeal. It is dormant during the day and uses the host’s skills while in control at night. A DC 20 Spot check reveals the extra shadow. Otherwise, detection requires telepathic contact. Dispel evil or an ethereal opponent can drive it out of its host.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +12, Concentration +8, Diplomacy +12, Gather Information +12, Hide +20, Intimidate +10, Knowledge (the planes) +12, Listen +12, Sense Motive +12, Spot +12. Alertness, Blind-Fight, Combat Reflexes.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land or underground. Solitary, always neutral evil, no treasure. Advances to 9–12 HD (Medium). Printed level adjustment +7.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The special attacks line says “Will drain.” The detailed ability drains Wisdom and uses a Will save.

lines: A bipedal rat with spined tentacles instead of forelimbs. Groups use their tentacles to immobilize prey.

gm.title: Other statistics

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Tentacle +4 melee (1d3 plus paralysis).
Full attack. Two tentacles +4 melee (1d3 plus paralysis each) and bite −1 melee (1d4).
Paralysis (Ex). Each tentacle hit requires a DC 12 Fortitude save or the target is paralyzed for 1d6+2 minutes.

gm.title: Traits and tactics
lines: Darkvision 60 ft. and scent. It usually attacks only if threatened, cornered, or hunting in a pack.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The grappling line explicitly gives +4 despite the creature’s Small size and Str 10. The print uses swarm as an organization label, with an individual Small aberration stat block.
