gm.title: Description
lines: A spirit driven from its living body by possession. Bands of the dispossessed sometimes gather in an abandoned home and act out their former lives.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Medium disembodied spirit of a living creature. Alignment varies.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Uncommon in the Shadow World. Appears in bands of 1d20. Active any time. No diet. Average intelligence 8–10. Medium, about 6 ft. tall. Morale 15–16. No treasure, bloodline, blood abilities, or magic resistance.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Touch of despair. One attack for 1d4 damage plus despair. When the cumulative number of hits equals the target’s Constitution, its spirit leaves and becomes one of the dispossessed. The attacker immediately takes over the body. If the target survives, despair lingers for one day per hit. Each casting of remove fear shortens this by one day.

gm.title: Depression
lines: On first sight of any dispossessed spirit, save vs. paralyzation. On failure, movement is halved and attacks and Dexterity-based tasks suffer −3 or −25% while any dispossessed spirit remains within 100 yards. After leaving that range, the penalty falls to −1 or −10% for 4d6 hours plus one hour for each four hours of exposure. A character conversing with one saves again each turn.

gm.title: Defenses and behavior
lines: Requires a +1 or better weapon to hit. As spirits of still-living bodies, they do not respond to holy water, turning, or attacks specific to undead. They can speak and move small or medium objects psychically. Evil spirits seize chances to possess others. Any spirit has a 60% chance to mistake a character for its old body and focus on that character. Restoring it to its own body, or the death of that original body, puts it to rest. Taking a different body offers no lasting relief.

gm.title: Seeming
lines: Perception none, Seeming slight. Observers with low Perception can mistake them for corporeal people.

gm.title: Description
lines: This sorrowsworn throws out its harpoon-like arms to pull distant creatures into reach.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing while in dim light or darkness.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Psychic Leech. At the start of the Lonely’s turn, each creature within 5 ft. must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom save or take 10 (3d6) psychic damage.
Thrives on Company. The Lonely has advantage on attack rolls when at least two other creatures are within 30 ft. Otherwise, it has disadvantage on attack rolls.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Harpoon Arm attack and use Sorrowful Embrace.
Harpoon Arm. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (4d8 + 3) piercing damage. It also grapples a Large or smaller creature (escape DC 15). The Lonely has two harpoon arms and can grapple up to two creatures at once.
Sorrowful Embrace. Every creature the Lonely has grappled makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure, it takes 18 (4d8) psychic damage. On a success, it takes half damage. Either way, the Lonely pulls each grappled creature up to 30 ft. directly toward itself.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: On its turn, a Dazed creature chooses only one: move, take an action, or take a bonus action. Becoming Dazed during its turn ends that turn. Extra actions from effects such as Haste or Action Surge remain available. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration can end Dazed. The GM can allow other remedies.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: The Fury called the Avenger closes in with claws and a scourge that saps strength.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any land or underground. Triune with her sisters. Always lawful evil. No treasure or level adjustment. Advances as a fighter. The text describes her as having the combat prowess of a 10th-level fighter.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +7. AC +3 Dex, +2 natural. Touch 13, flat-footed 12. Base attack +10, printed grapple +1. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +8, Ref +5, Will +4.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +13, Diplomacy +12, Gather Information +13, Intimidate +14, Listen +13, Sense Motive +13, Spot +13. Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Exotic Weapon Proficiency, Flyby Attack.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +13 melee for 1d4 + 3, bite +11 melee for 1d4 + 3, or +3 scourge of weakness +16 ranged for 1d4 + 8 and Strength damage.
Full attack as printed. Two claws +13 melee for 1d4 + 3 each, one bite +11 melee for 1d4 + 3, or one scourge strike. The prose allows a mixed round. For a mixed full attack, substitute one scourge strike for one claw.
Scourge of weakness. A strike deals 1d3 Strength damage unless the target succeeds on a DC 15 Fortitude save.
See Fury shared rules for Rake and Breath Weapon.

gm.title: Fury shared rules
lines:
Printed source. Furies, pp. 79–80. The sisters appear together and speak all humanoid languages. They try three times to divert a target from atonement before trying to kill them in public.
Defenses. Damage reduction 15/good. Immune to paralysis, polymorph, and mind-affecting effects.
Scourge. The +3 scourge works like a whip that deals 1d4 lethal damage before modifiers. A Fury may substitute it for her claw attacks. Use the attack and ability damage listed for that sister. Rake (Ex) is +9 melee for 1d4 + 1 damage.
Alter Self (Sp). At will as a standard action, a Fury can take the form of an elderly human woman indefinitely. Caster level 10.
Breath Weapon (Su, 3/day). Fill one adjacent square with foul air. Apply stinking cloud as cast by an 8th-level sorcerer, with a DC 16 Fortitude save.
Find Penitent (Su). Furies can locate a target who seeks redemption at the invitation or embrace stage of corruption. The target cannot hide from them, even with magic.
Gaseous Death (Su). At 0 HP, a Fury and her scourge dissolve into smoke. Surviving sisters continue to fight, though the last survivor tries to flee. If a sister survives, the slain Furies return at full HP after 24 hours. To kill them permanently, all three must die within the same 24 hours and an Innocent must deal the killing blows. Their scourges remain after permanent death.
Weaknesses. A good cleric or a paladin can turn each Fury separately by invoking her true name. A turning attempt cannot destroy, rebuke, or command her. A Fury cannot deliberately harm a good creature except with her breath weapon.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The full-attack line presents the attack modes as alternatives, but the prose allows her to use her scourge and claws in the same round without specifying a routine. The mixed full attack is a table ruling. The stat line calls the scourge rider Strength drain. The combat prose supplies Strength damage and the save. The printed grapple +1 and Hit Dice formula are retained.

lines: The Void hollows out this fey until little remains but ribbonlike skin. A metal ring bound to the creature shields it and conducts the energy inside it.

lines: Ring Shield. Perception 13, Stealth 14. Vulnerable to radiant, slashing, and thunder damage. Resistant to bludgeoning and necrotic damage, Charmed, and Unconscious. Darkvision 60 ft. Languages Common and Void Speech. Telepathy 60 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Fey Resilience. Resistance to Charmed and Unconscious.
Magic Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Ring Shield. The bound ring works as a standard shield. If dropped or taken, it teleports back at the start of the tollinvardo’s next turn. When the tollinvardo dies, the ring is destroyed in a burst of sparks. Each creature within 10 ft. of the ring must pass a DC 14 Dexterity save or be Blinded until the end of its next turn.

lines:
Multiattack. Use Ring Shield, then make two Voidstaff attacks.

Ring Shield. Throw the ring at up to two visible creatures within 60 ft. before it vanishes and returns. Each makes a DC 14 Dexterity save, taking 7 (2d6) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines:
Glimpse Between. One visible creature within 10 ft. must pass a DC 14 Wisdom save or be Frightened until the end of its next turn.
Restrictive Shroud. One visible creature within 60 ft. makes a DC 14 Strength save. Failure halves its speed and imposes disadvantage on attack rolls and Strength and Dexterity checks and saves for 1 minute. Repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect. The tollinvardo can bind only one creature at a time.

gm.title: Reactions

lines: A shelled coastal humanoid. In a group, the front line withdraws into its shells while the rear line shoots, then emerges when the volleys stop.

lines: An opalescent snail chews through barriers and leaves false paths in the Labyrinth. Skilled handlers sometimes train one as a mount for passing through magical wards.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 11, Stealth 10. Resistant to Exhaustion and Frightened. Immune to force damage. Keensense 60 ft. No languages.

gm.title: Ability modifiers

Dispelling Slime. When the snail deals force damage to a creature under a magical effect, there is a 25% chance to end that effect as Dispel Magic without an ability check. Standing on or chewing a magic item other than an artifact for 1 minute gives a 10% chance of suppressing the item’s magic for 24 hours, disabling activation. A sentient item keeps its awareness and normal means of communication.
Monstrosity Resilience. Resistance to Exhaustion and Frightened.
Rainbow Ward. A creature within 30 ft. that relies on sight has disadvantage on attack rolls against the snail.
Path Maker. At the end of its turn, the snail can deal 9 (2d8) force damage to an object or structure sharing its space, ignoring any damage threshold. Magical barriers such as Wall of Force count as difficult terrain for it. It suffers no other penalties from moving through or starting its turn in a magical barrier’s space.

gm.title: Reactions

gm.title: Description
lines: A dryad corrupted by a night hag can seize a living tree and attack from inside it. The tree decays while the skinner lives within.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Perception 14, Stealth 16. Vulnerable to radiant damage. Resists cold, fire, lightning, and poison damage, plus bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks. Immune to Charmed. Darkvision 60 ft. Languages Abyssal, Elvish, Infernal, Sylvan.

lines:

lines:

If reduced to 15 HP, the tree dies and the skinner appears within 5 ft. of it or in the nearest unoccupied space. The skinner can also exit as a bonus action to the nearest unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the tree, returning it to object status. After at most three days of occupation, the tree dies.
Squeeze (tree form only). A creature the skinner is Grappling makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure it cannot breathe or cast spells with verbal components until the Grapple ends.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim illumination while retaining color and detail.
Scent. Detect opponents by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double those ranges and overpowering odors triple them. A move action identifies the direction of a scent. At 5 ft. or closer, pinpoint the source.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Environment. Temperate plains. Organization. Solitary, pair, or herd (5–8). It is about 25 ft. long and can weigh about 20,000 lb. The combat prose favors charging larger intruders and trampling smaller opponents. Treasure none. Advancement. 17–32 HD (Huge), 33–48 HD (Gargantuan). Level adjustment none listed.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines:
Powerful Charge (Ex). A Gore made as part of a charge deals 4d8 + 20 damage. Apply the usual charge modifiers.
Trample (Ex). As a full-round action, move up to twice speed, or 60 ft., and run over opponents at least one size smaller. A creature is trampled when the triceratops covers its whole space. Deal 2d12 + 15 bludgeoning damage once per target per round. A trampled opponent can make an attack of opportunity at −4, or attempt a DC 28 Reflex save for half. A partially covered larger space permits the −4 attack of opportunity without trampling. If it ends in an illegal space, return it to its most recent legal position or the nearest legal position if closer.

If the triceratops bugles before beginning the 20-ft. charge movement, the charge target has disadvantage on the Wisdom save. If it then fails the charge’s Strength save, the triceratops can Stomp the prone target without spending another bonus action.

gm.title: Description
lines: A detached troll arm that crawls and lashes out under its parent’s direction.

gm.title: Severing and reattachment
lines:
When the troll takes 15 or more slashing damage from a single instance, roll a d20. On 1–10 no part is severed. On 11–14 it loses a leg if any remain. On 15–18 it loses an arm if any remain. On 19–20 it is decapitated. It survives the decapitation if it can regenerate. If the troll dies after decapitation, its severed head also dies.
A detached part acts on the troll’s initiative with its own movement and action. If the troll finishes a short or long rest before reattaching the part, a replacement grows and the old part dies. The sidebar gives no reattachment action or timing.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Regeneration. The part regains 10 HP at the start of its turn. Acid or fire damage prevents that healing at the start of its next turn. Applying the troll’s Regeneration to the part, it dies when it begins its turn at 0 HP and cannot regenerate.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Claw. Make one Claw attack on the arm’s turn using the parent Troll’s attack. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage. The attack has disadvantage unless the troll can see both the arm and its target.

gm.title: Effects on the troll
lines: Each lost arm removes one Claw attack from the troll’s Multiattack. Losing its head removes Bite, and the body is Blinded unless the head can see it. With one leg missing, halve the troll’s speed. With both legs missing, it falls Prone and can crawl if it has one or both arms. Halve its speed if it has only one arm to crawl with. With no arms or legs left, its speed is 0 and speed bonuses cannot increase it.

gm.title: Parent encounter
lines: Use this procedure only with the Troll (variant). The sidebar gives each part its own AC, HP, movement and any listed attack. It gives no separate size, ability scores, challenge rating or XP. The DM decides how to resolve checks or saves the sidebar leaves unspecified.

gm.title: Printed source

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Description
lines: This ragged, foul-smelling cloaker rides a living host until it can drain another victim. It keeps a dead host as a puppet.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +7. AC 21 (printed breakdown −1 size, +3 Dex, +7 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 16. Base attack +2. Space 10 ft., reach 10 ft. (5 ft. with bite). Fort unlisted, Ref +5, Will +7. Hide +12, Listen +11, Spot +11. Alertness, Improved Initiative. Underground. Solitary. Standard treasure. Always chaotic evil. Advancement 6–8 HD (Large), 9–16 HD (Huge).

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Tail slap +8 melee (1d6+5).
Full attack. Tail slap +8 melee (1d6+5) and bite +3 melee (1d4+2). It can use its tail on other creatures while engulfing.
Attach (Su). After engulfing a human-shaped creature at least one size smaller, it attempts to bite. A hit attaches the cloaker, which can allow the host to move freely after it stops struggling. It loses its bite while attached. Death ward protects a creature against attachment and removes an attached cloaker. The cloaker also detaches if it is destroyed or successfully turned.
Forcible removal. Use the Attach procedure: another character makes a DC 15 Strength check to tear the cloaker free. On success the host gains 1d4 negative levels. The cloaker survives and follows its hostless rules.
Energy Drain (Su). When the host touches a living creature, that creature gains 1 negative level. Use a touch attack if the target resists. If the host touches no living creature over 24 hours, the cloaker instead gives the host 1 negative level. Fortitude DC 14 removes each negative level at the normal recovery check.
Create Spawn (Su). A humanoid killed by the drain rises in 24 hours as a zombie without its living abilities. Zombies remain controlled until the cloaker dies. It stays attached to a dead host and controls that host once it rises.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Undead traits and DR 10/magic. Without a host it loses 1 HD each week until destroyed. Once it attaches, it regains 1 HD for each day it feeds.

gm.title: Shared dread cloaker rules
lines:
Printed source. Cloaker, Dread, p. 51.
Damage reduction (Su). A cloaker draped around its host shares its damage reduction against physical attacks other than area attacks.
Engulf (Ex). As a standard action, the cloaker envelops a creature at least one size category smaller. Its host is engulfed automatically. Any other target requires a successful grapple check without provoking an attack of opportunity. The target is pinned. A cloaker without a host gains +4 to bite the engulfed creature.
Split damage from attacks that hit an engulfing cloaker equally between it and its victim. Area spells deal full damage to both. A shadow or undead cloaker can still strike other targets with its tail while engulfing a creature.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed AC breakdown adds to 19, but the total is 21. Use the printed total, touch, and flat-footed values. The stat block omits grapple and Fortitude. If needed, the standard 3.5 statistics yield grapple +11 and Fortitude +1 against effects that apply to undead. The combat paragraph requires DC 17 and says removal kills the cloaker. The detailed Attach ability instead specifies DC 15 and provides rules for a hostless cloaker. Use the Attach procedure as a table ruling.

gm.title: Description
lines: The leafless ruler of a corrupt grove pins travelers under its branches to feed through its roots.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative −2. Printed AC components −2 size, −1 Dex, +13 natural. Touch AC 7, flat-footed AC 21. Base attack +4, grapple +21. Space 10 ft., reach 15 ft. Fort +0, Ref +1, Will +4.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +21 melee (1d6 + 9). Full attack. Two slams +2 melee (1d6 + 9 each) as printed. A full attack deals double damage to an object or structure.
Trample (Ex). 2d12 + 5 damage, Reflex DC 23 for half.
Blood Drain (Ex). On its next turn after pinning a living foe, 1d3 roots attach. Each root drains 1 Constitution each round it maintains the grapple. It cannot move while feeding and takes a full-round action to become mobile again. Break the pin normally or sever every attached root. Each root has AC 15 and 4 HP independent of the treant. Use Ravenloft vampire feeding rules from chapter 5 of the Ravenloft Player’s Handbook for its feeding needs.
Spells. It casts as a 6th-level druid and chooses no spells that employ fire.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Undead traits, damage reduction 10/slashing, and fire vulnerability. It has lost the living treant’s ability to animate trees.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Hide −10, Intimidate +8, one Knowledge skill +8, Listen +9, Sense Motive +9, Spot +9, Survival +9. Hide has a +16 racial bonus in dead or dying forest. Feats: Cleave, Improved Sunder, Iron Will, Power Attack.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any forest. Solitary or with 4–7 dread treants. Always neutral evil. Standard treasure. Advances to 9–17 HD (Huge) or 18–22 HD (Gargantuan).

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed full attack is +2 while its single slam is +21. For a consistent table ruling, use +21 for both slams.
The printed AC components do not add to AC 20, and Dexterity 6 gives a −2 modifier rather than the printed −1 in those components. Use the listed total, touch, and flat-footed values.

gm.title: Description
lines: A white unicorn with golden strands in its mane and tail. Its humanoid form is a young knight in white chain mail.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural AC 2. In humanoid form the chain mail gives AC 3. Magic resistance 15%. Exceptional intelligence 15–16. Fearless morale 19–20.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Sense true enemies within 240 yards. Both forms are immune to charm, hold and poison, and make other saves as an 11th-level wizard. The white mail vanishes if taken off. The servant must spend one full turn in natural form before the armor can reappear.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Hooves and horn, natural form. Make two hoof attacks at 1d6 damage each and a horn attack at 1d12. The horn attack gets +2 to hit. If the unicorn has 30 feet to build up speed, it can charge with only the horn for 3d12 damage. The horn's touch dispels magic as an 11th-level wizard.
Longsword, humanoid form. Make two attacks per round with a +2 longsword that dispels magic as the horn does.

gm.title: Bearer benefits
lines: No bearer is named. Tradition says the servant is granted to a fair and just human or elven maiden. The bearer can sense true enemies and gains the servant's spell immunities while in contact with it.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Description
lines: A lion-headed exile from Carceri, with white claws, red scales, and quills for a mane. It sometimes spends a year in the mortal world before returning home.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Common in Carceri and very rare elsewhere. Solitary carnivore. Exceptional intelligence (15–16). Treasure F, R, X. Champion morale (15–16). Height 11–14 feet. 120-foot infravision. Speaks Utukku and can communicate telepathically with intelligent creatures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws and bite. Two claw attacks at 4d4 each and one bite at 3d4.
At will. Detect invisibility, read languages, know alignment, and detect magic.
Three times per day each. Teleport without error carrying up to 1,500 pounds, cause fear as a wand of fear, create darkness in a 30-foot radius, and produce a 12d6 lightning bolt.
Once per day each. Symbol of discord and control weather as an 18th-level mage.
Once per week each. Cause disease by touch and polymorph self into a human or humanoid form for a full day.

gm.title: Defenses
lines: Only weapons with a magical bonus of +1 or higher can hit. 50% magic resistance. Lightning, fire, and poisonous gas deal half damage on a failed save or one-quarter on success. Add +4 to saves vs. poison. Immune to mental probes such as ESP and telepathy.

gm.title: Travel and Red Curse
lines: Once a century the utukku can plane shift from Carceri to the Prime Material Plane. After one year it returns automatically with up to 4,000 pounds of material. It neither gains Legacies nor requires cinnabryl.

gm.title: Description
lines: An undead ruler watches over its plunder and commands the warriors buried with it.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Perception 13, Stealth 12. Resists cold damage. Immune to necrotic and poison damage and to Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, and Poisoned. Darkvision 60 ft., truesight 30 ft. Languages known in life.

Aura of Authority. Allies within 10 ft. have advantage on attacks and saves while the buried lord is free of the Incapacitated condition.
Grave Goods Sense. Pinpoint anyone wearing or carrying its belongings or grave goods within 60 ft. and sense the direction of those objects within 1 mile.
Rejuvenation. After destruction, return at full HP in a new body 24 hours later, in a random unoccupied space within 100 ft. of the spot where it fell. Putting it to rest, usually by returning its remains to its burial mound, prevents this.

gm.title: Actions

Repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effect. A success grants immunity to this buried lord’s gaze for 24 hours.

2/day: Bane.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Parry. Add 2 AC against one melee attack that would hit. The buried lord must see its attacker and wield a melee weapon or hold a shield.

gm.title: Description
lines: A pond-dwelling predator uses supernatural thirst to draw creatures to the water. It can also leave eggs close to where they drink.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 14, Stealth 16. Resists poison damage and the Poisoned and Prone conditions. Immune to Blinded and Exhaustion. Keensense 60 ft., its maximum sensing range. No languages.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +8, Dex +0, Con +7, Int -3, Wis +1, Cha -3

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. It breathes air and water.
Aura of Thirst. At the start of the vallowex’s turn, creatures within 30 ft. make a DC 15 Constitution save. On failure, each has disadvantage on its next attack roll or ability check before the vallowex’s next turn starts. Each minute in the aura adds one level of Exhaustion. A creature can remove a level by spending an action to drink a pint of water. Creatures immune to Exhaustion ignore the aura.
Infested Water. After every seven days it spends in an enclosed body of water up to 100 ft. in radius, it deposits eggs. They remain viable for 24 hours. A DC 15 Intelligence (Nature) check to inspect the water spots them. A Beast or Humanoid who drinks the water makes a DC 15 Constitution save or contracts a disease. Only one tadpole can mature per host. After each long rest, the host repeats the save. On failure, reduce its Strength score by 1d4. The reduction lasts until a long rest after the disease is cured. If Strength reaches 0, the host dies and a vallowex emerges. Three successful saves or a magical cure destroy the tadpole.
Underwater Camouflage. Its Stealth is 21 underwater.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Spiked Tongue and two Tail attacks. Swallow can replace Spiked Tongue.
Spiked Tongue. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing. The target is Grappled, escape DC 15, and Restrained for the duration. The vallowex cannot use Spiked Tongue on someone else while the Grapple holds.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 16 (2d10 + 5) bludgeoning.
Swallow. Use Spiked Tongue on a Medium or smaller creature it is Grappling. On a hit, the creature is swallowed and the Grapple ends. It is Blinded and Restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects originating outside the vallowex, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the vallowex’s turns. Only one creature can be swallowed. If that creature deals at least 15 damage to the vallowex during one turn, the vallowex makes a DC 15 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On failure it regurgitates the target, which lands Prone within 5 ft. If the vallowex dies, the swallowed creature is no longer Restrained and can exit Prone by spending 10 ft. of movement.

gm.title: Description
lines: Victor Mordenheim is the Lamordian surgeon who built Adam. He works in Schloss Mordenheim, where his machines keep his injured wife Elise von Brandthofen alive.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A lean, pale man who looks to be in his thirties, with prematurely grey hair, tired blue eyes and a faint scar on his forehead. He wears plain brown wool or a surgical gown.

gm.title: What brought him here
lines: Victor raised Adam as a son and tried to teach him to live among people. Adam attacked Elise von Brandthofen, vanished with Eva, and left Victor to save what remained of his wife.

gm.title: What he wants
lines: Victor wants a new body for Elise von Brandthofen. He will rob graves and comb hospices for suitable remains. Locals blame him for disappearances that Adam causes.

gm.title: Running Victor
lines: He rarely starts a fight and has no weapon training. He can make one attack with whatever weapon he has. Its damage depends on the weapon.

gm.title: Shared curse
lines: Victor cannot die while Adam lives. He shares Adam’s hit point total and can regrow from a surviving piece of his body.
Adam feels pain inflicted on Victor. If Victor’s body is completely destroyed, his spirit seeks a recently dead human man. The body takes on Victor’s appearance within a week.

gm.title: Psionic Powers (MCDM)
lines: Powers are supernatural and have no components. Antimagic Field, Counterspell, and Dispel Magic affect spells or magic and do not stop powers. A creature with a melee power attack can use it for an opportunity attack.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

lines:

Driving Hunger. A creature that starts its turn in the swarm’s space or within 10 ft. of it makes a DC 16 Constitution save. On a failure, it must spend a bonus action on its next turn eating or searching for food.
Swarm. Creatures can occupy the swarm’s space and it can occupy theirs. It can pass through any opening that admits a Tiny mite. It cannot regain HP or gain temporary HP.

gm.title: Description
lines: A vampire’s chosen companion survives an interrupted Dark Kiss. The vorlog charms a replacement and drains their Wisdom to keep them devoted.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +6. AC components +2 Dex, +3 natural, +4 chain shirt. Touch AC 12, flat-footed AC 17. Base attack +6, grapple +10. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +7, Ref +4, Will +3.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack and full attack as printed. Unarmed strike +10/+5 melee (1d3 + 4 nonlethal and Wisdom Drain), short sword +10/+5 melee (1d6 + 4, 19–20/×2), or masterwork mighty longbow +9 ranged (1d8 + 4, 19–20/×2).
Animal Rage (Su). At will, animals within 50 ft. make a DC 14 Will save or rage as the spell at caster level 12 and attack the nearest creature, even the vorlog.
Charm Person (Sp). At will at caster level 6, Will DC 12.
Wisdom Drain (Su). The unarmed hit deals 1d3 Wisdom damage to a living target. At Wisdom below 3 it becomes a lost one under the vorlog’s control. The vorlog keeps its surrogate at or below half their normal Wisdom.

gm.title: Traits
lines: DR 5/silver and magic. Immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, sleep, and paralysis. Fast Healing (Ex) restores 1 HP per hour while at 1 HP or more, or 1 HP per round if the surrogate is physically present. At 0 HP or less it becomes a puddle of tears, moves at speed 20 ft., can climb walls and pass through tiny cracks, and must reach a dark haven in 1d4 hours or evaporate. After resting 8 hours it resumes humanoid form. Direct sunlight deals 1d6 damage each round. It will not approach a good deity’s holy symbol presented with conviction. It needs food and Wisdom and dies after three months without a surrogate.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Climb +16, Craft (bowmaking) +4, Diplomacy +3, Listen +4, Move Silently +13, Ride +4, Spot +4. Alertness, Blind-Fight, Dodge, Improved Critical (short sword), Improved Initiative, Improved Unarmed Strike, Point Blank Shot, Power Attack.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land and underground. Solitary. Usually chaotic, always evil. Standard treasure. Gear includes 50 +1 arrows and a ring of climbing. It retains its former languages. A charmed victim who drinks the vorlog’s blood for three consecutive nights becomes its surrogate.

gm.title: Template for another encounter
lines: Apply to a humanoid or monstrous humanoid. Keep type, size, speed, attacks, damage, saves, and existing special abilities. Increase Hit Dice one die size to a maximum of d12. Add +3 natural armor, +4 Str, +2 Dex, +2 Cha, and a +8 racial bonus to Move Silently. Add Alertness and Improved Unarmed Strike if missing. Add the vorlog attacks, traits and weaknesses above. Animal Rage Will DC is 10 + half the vorlog’s HD + Cha modifier. Charm Person Will DC is 11 + Cha modifier. CR is base +1, level adjustment base +8, and advancement by class.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The sample prints iterative melee bonuses in both Attack and Full Attack and gives the longbow a 19–20/×2 critical. Listed values follow the printing. The sample’s level adjustment is +15.

gm.title: Description
lines: This fledgling was a human warrior. It puts victims into a fever sleep and can flee as a swarm.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Fledgling sample, 5th-level human warrior. Initiative +9. AC components +5 Dex, +5 natural, +1 deflection. Touch 16, flat-footed 16. Base attack +5, grapple +11. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +4, Ref +8, Will +4.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +11 melee for 1d4 + 6 and filth fever.
Full attack. Two of the listed claws.
Fever Sleep (Su). Standard action against one target within 30 ft. who meets its eyes. Will DC 12 or sleep as the spell at caster level 12 without a Hit Dice limit. Feeding does not awaken the target.
Blood Drain (Ex). Pin a living creature in a grapple. Each round the pin is maintained, drain 1d4 Constitution and gain 5 temporary HP. A victim must also save against filth fever.
Filth fever (Ex). Any living victim damaged by a claw or blood drain makes a DC 12 Fortitude save. Incubation is 1d3 days. The disease deals 1d3 Dexterity and 1d3 Constitution damage.
Children of the Night (Su). Once per day as a standard action, call 6d10 HD of monstrous vermin. They arrive after 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 5/iron and magic in the sample’s stat line. Cold and electricity resistance 10, turn resistance +3, spider climb, and undead traits.
Disease (Ex). The strain carries one permanent disease. It also picks up injury- or contact-transmitted diseases when it feeds on an infected victim. Add its Cha modifier to the disease DC. Each secondary disease’s DC falls by 1 each day after acquisition. At DC 0 it loses that disease. A DC 15 Heal check identifies diseases it carries.
Alternate Form (Su). As a standard action, use polymorph at caster level 12 to change into a dire rat, a rat swarm, or a swarm of Fine vermin until changing again or until sunrise. A swarm has as many 1-HP members as the vampire has total HP. Each member killed costs the vampire 1 HP. The swarm members still carry its diseases.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: A humanoid or monstrous humanoid killed by its disease rises as vampire spawn 1d4 days after burial. A victim drained to Constitution 0 returns as spawn if it had 4 or fewer HD or as a vrykolaka if it had 5 or more. A creator controls its spawn until it dies.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines:
Garlic, anise, a continuous line of aniseed, and a strongly brandished holy symbol keep it away. It cannot enter an immaculate room or cross running water unaided. Still or stagnant water does not trouble it.
Direct sunlight leaves it with a single move or attack action. It is destroyed in the next round if it cannot escape the light. Immersion in running water takes away one-third of its HP each round and destroys it at the end of round 3. A vampire strain whose base creature has a swim speed retains it and escapes the immersion weakness.
At 1 HP or more it heals 5 HP per round. At 0 HP or less it flees as a swarm. At least half the swarm must get to its coffin within 2 hours or it is destroyed. After 1 hour there it reaches 1 HP and resumes healing.
An iron spike through its skull kills it while the spike remains. Burn the body completely to keep it from returning. A casting of remove disease forces a Fortitude save or bestows two negative levels. While it sleeps in its coffin or is incapacitated it automatically fails this save. It is destroyed permanently at negative levels equal to or greater than its HD. When destroyed, it dissolves into vapors like stinking cloud at caster level 12.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +8, Handle Animal +4, Hide +13, Intimidate +6, Jump +12, Listen +13, Move Silently +13, Search +6, Sense Motive +11, Spot +13. Alertness, Blind-Fight, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Power Attack, Run.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any environment in Ravenloft. Solitary, pair, or gang of 2–5. An organized group can contain 1–2 full vampires and 2–5 vampire spawn. Speaks languages known in life. Always evil. Standard treasure. The printed warrior wears a ring of protection +1.

gm.title: Template and age
lines: Apply the strain to a humanoid or monstrous humanoid using the 3.5 vampire template as the base. Keep its size, base attack, saves, skill points, d12 HD and applicable original powers. Constitution is absent. These age entries give the changes to Str, Dex, Int, Wis, Cha, speed, natural AC and Outcast Rating (OR) against non-vrykolakas. Intelligence has a minimum of 3. Every age tier requires cold iron and magic to bypass damage reduction. Apply one age row only. The sample already incorporates its age. For unlisted save DCs use 10 + half HD, rounded down, + Cha modifier. Filth fever uses 12 + Cha modifier instead. Claw damage follows the size table if the base creature has no claw attack. gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: A dancing light that reaches Cerilia just ahead of an opening Shadow World portal. It draws vitality from the living before the portal pulls it back.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Tiny to Small floating creature. Chaotic neutral.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Rare in Cerilia and the Shadow World. Solitary, appearing 1d3. Active at night in Cerilia or any time in the Shadow World. Feeds on Cerilian life energy. High intelligence 13–14. Treasure Q. Size 1–4 ft. across. Morale 15–16. No bloodline, blood abilities, or Perception. Seeming lesser.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Life drain. One touch for 2d8 damage to a Cerilian creature. It feeds on that loss without adding the damage to its own HP. A non-Cerilian takes a 1d8 burn instead and provides no nourishment.

gm.title: Feeding near the portal
lines: When Cerilian characters are within a quarter mile, there is a 50% chance the creature feeds on their life energy rather than the surroundings. Affected Cerilians save vs. poison or take 2d6 damage. When Cerilians are on the Shadow World side of a portal about to open and a will o’Shadow is present, make that save with a 1-point penalty. It is normally invisible on that side of the portal.

gm.title: Defenses and tactics
lines: Mundane weapon blows deal normal damage. Detect invisibility and shadow magic are the only magic specifically noted as effective. Magical light makes the creature invisible until the light goes out. Its lesser Seeming can camouflage it with blur, color spray, dancing lights, or hypnotic pattern. It usually avoids direct combat, attacks to replace lost energy when provoked, and tries to flee at 5 HP or fewer.

gm.title: Portal clues
lines: One to three lights can precede a portal by 1 minute to 3 hours. A larger light means it is closer to opening. Nearby vegetation may stay wilted for 1d4 days per round the portal was open. The lights communicate with one another through their movement.

Bite and tail. Bite for 2d8 and lash with the tail for 1d8. Treat its Strength as 20 when grabbing or holding something.
Roll over. With enough room, it can roll onto up to three human-sized or smaller targets. Save vs. paralysis to avoid it. On failure, take 1d4 damage per wurmling Hit Die. It can remain on top for the same damage each subsequent round. On a failed initial save, each of the victim’s possessions must save vs. crushing blow or be destroyed.

gm.title: Defenses
lines: Magic resistance 2% per HD. Immune to scarlet pimpernel hallucinations and mood-altering abilities or proficiencies such as fast talk, intimidation, and bardic charm. Add +3 to saves against mind-altering spells and mind-affecting Legacies.

gm.title: Skills and Red Curse
lines: As a thief of level equal to its HD, it can open locks, find and remove traps, move silently, hear noise, and read languages. It knows one spoken language per 2 HD. It has legend lore and local history, plus information-related nonweapon proficiencies as a thief of the same level. Gain Legacies as an Inheritor of level equal to HD. A 10 HD specimen has five Legacies, a 12 HD specimen has six, and a 15 HD specimen has seven. The first needs no crimson essence. Later Legacies need crimson essence to activate at acquisition and stay permanently. It needs cinnabryl to maintain them. Typical choices are Anti-Poison, Crimson Fire, Digging, Farsight, Red Shield, Shape Stone, and Temperature, or choices suited to Eusdria.

gm.title: Hit point rule

lines: A two-legged dragon with leathery wings, rocky indigo scales and a hooked tail stinger.

lines: Armor class 13 + PB. Strength save +3 + PB. Perception +2 + PB. Acid damage immunity. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 12 + PB.

gm.title: Caregiver scaling
lines: PB is the caregiver’s proficiency bonus.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Learning to Fly. The wyvern has a flying speed of 10 × PB feet.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Signature Attack (Stinger). Melee weapon attack at +3 + PB, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1d6 + PB piercing damage.

gm.title: Ferocity actions
lines:
Level 1, Acidic Sting (2 Ferocity). Make a signature attack at 15-ft. reach. A hit deals extra acid damage equal to PB.
Level 3, Liquefied Meal (5 Ferocity). A Large or smaller creature within 5 ft. makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB. On a failure it falls Prone and takes 1d4 + PB acid damage. The wyvern gains temporary hit points equal to the acid damage dealt.
Level 5, Tail Sweep (8 Ferocity). Every creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a Strength save against DC 10 + PB. On a failure it takes PBd6 bludgeoning damage and is pushed up to 10 ft. away.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Enraged Protector. When a visible creature within 30 ft. of the wyvern drops its caregiver to 0 HP or scores a critical hit against the caregiver, the wyvern can move up to its speed. If it ends within 5 ft. of that attacker, it can make a signature attack against it.

gm.title: Mystic connection
lines: Acid-Enhanced. At 9th level, a Beastheart with this companion and Mystic Connection can spend a bonus action once per long rest to exude acid from their hands for 1 minute. Their melee weapon attacks and unarmed strikes deal an extra 1d8 acid damage during this time.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Statistics

gm.title: Other statistics

gm.title: Traits
lines: It cannot speak in either form. In natural form it uses hisses and growls, and both forms retain the telepathic link with its bearer.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

Claws, humanoid form. Two claw attacks deal 1d6 damage apiece.

gm.title: Bearer benefits
lines: The Margrave of Slagovich can use poison three times per day as the reverse of the priest spell neutralize poison. This power works regardless of telepathic contact or whether the bearer carries the coat of arms.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

lines: Summoning this elemental from the Plane of Earth raises the ground into an armored reptile. Its steps can level buildings, and it can draw into its shell to recover.

lines: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/Day). When it fails a saving throw, the zaratan can choose to succeed instead.
Siege Monster. It deals double damage to objects and structures. Earth-Shaking Movement already includes this increase.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Stomp attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (4d8 + 10) force damage.
Stomp. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 26 (3d10 + 10) thunder damage.
Spit Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +17 to hit, range 120/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 31 (6d8 + 10) force damage.
Spew Debris (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cube makes a DC 25 Dexterity save, taking 33 (6d10) bludgeoning damage on a failure or half as much on a success. A creature that fails by 5 or more is also knocked prone.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Earth-Shaking Movement. After moving at least 10 ft. on the ground, the zaratan creates a shock wave across a 120-ft.-radius circle centered on itself. That ground is difficult terrain for 1 minute. Each concentrating creature on the ground there loses concentration unless it passes a DC 25 Constitution save. Structures touching the ground in the area take 100 thunder damage. A creature within half the height of a collapsing structure makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 17 (5d6) bludgeoning damage, falls prone, and is trapped and restrained in the rubble. A successful save halves the damage and avoids the collapse’s prone and restrained effects. A buried creature can use an action to escape with a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check. An adjacent helper within 5 ft. can spend an action clearing debris to grant advantage on the check. With three helpers spending their actions, the check succeeds automatically.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The zaratan has 3 legendary actions. Use one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn, spending the listed action cost. Spent legendary actions return at the start of the creature's turn. A creature cannot use these actions while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using them.
Stomp (1 Action). Make one Stomp attack.
Move (1 Action). Move up to its speed.
Spit (2 Actions). Make one Spit Rock attack.
Retract (2 Actions). Withdraw into its shell. Until it emerges, the zaratan is restrained and has resistance to all damage. Its next legendary action must be Revitalize or Emerge.
Revitalize (2 Actions). Only while retracted, regain 52 (5d20) HP. The next legendary action must be Emerge.
Emerge (2 Actions). Only while retracted, leave the shell and make one Spit Rock attack.

gm.title: Description
lines: A zaratan resembles an immense stone turtle. Its movements shake the ground and topple structures.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Elemental Nature. The zaratan needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). It can choose to succeed on a failed saving throw.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical.
Siege Monster. It deals double damage to objects and structures. The damage to structures in Earth-Shaking Movement already includes this trait.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Earth-Shaking Movement. After moving at least 10 ft. on the ground, the zaratan can send a shock wave through the ground in a 120-ft. radius centered on it. The affected area becomes difficult terrain for 1 minute. A concentrating creature on the ground makes a DC 25 Constitution save or loses concentration.
Each structure in the area in contact with the ground takes 100 thunder damage. When one collapses, each creature within a distance equal to half the structure's height makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. On a failure it takes 17 (5d6) bludgeoning damage, falls prone, and is restrained by the rubble. On a success it takes half damage and avoids both conditions.
A buried creature can use an action to attempt a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check to escape. A helper within 5 ft. can use an action to clear rubble and grant advantage on the check. If three helpers do so, the check succeeds automatically.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Stomp attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (4d8 + 10) piercing damage.
Stomp. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 26 (3d10 + 10) bludgeoning damage.
Spit Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +17 to hit, range 120/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 31 (6d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage.
Spew Debris (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cube makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Deal 33 (6d10) bludgeoning damage on a failure or half on a success. A creature that fails by 5 or more also falls prone.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The zaratan has 3 legendary actions. It can use one option at the end of another creature's turn and recovers all spent actions at the start of its turn.
Stomp (1 action). Make one Stomp attack.
Move (1 action). Move up to its speed.
Spit (2 actions). Use Spit Rock.
Retract (2 actions). Withdraw into its shell. It is restrained and has resistance to all damage until it uses Emerge. Its next legendary action must be Revitalize or Emerge.
Revitalize (2 actions). While retracted, regain 52 (5d20) hit points. Its next legendary action must be Emerge.
Emerge (2 actions). While retracted, leave the shell and use Spit Rock.

DDAL04-01 - The Suits of the Mists

gm.title: Description
lines: This green-lit fog drifts over graves after dark. Its cadavers draw attention away from the cloud itself, which feeds on the dying.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any land. Solitary. Always neutral evil. No treasure. Advancement 7–12 HD (Colossal). It does not communicate.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative −2. AC −2 Dex, −8 size, and +12 deflection. Touch 12, flat-footed 14. No base attack or grapple listed. Printed space 60 ft., reach 0 ft. Fort +2, Ref +2, Will +5.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 15/magic, SR 12, and undead traits. The cloud fills an area 25 ft. square and 10 ft. deep per HD.
Vaporous (Ex). Passes through tiny cracks, makes no movement noise, cannot enter liquids, and automatically fails saves against damaging air or wind effects. The cloud gives concealment at 5 ft. and total concealment beyond 5 ft. Its cadavers can see through it.
Unnatural Aura (Su). Animals refuse to approach within 30 ft. and panic while inside that range if forced to enter.
Daylight Powerlessness (Ex). In natural sunlight the fog hangs motionless and its cadavers drop lifeless until sundown. A daylight spell does not have this effect.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Animate Cadaver (Su). Animate humanoid corpses inside the cloud, even buried corpses unless blessed at burial or interred in sanctified ground. Raise up to 10 per round, including previously defeated cadavers at full HP. The number active at once cannot exceed the fog’s current HP.
Despair (Su). A creature that sees the fog makes a DC 13 Fear save or stays shaken until it has spent 10 minutes completely out of sight. Whatever the result, that fog cannot affect it with despair again for one day.
Life Drain (Su). A creature at negative HP in the cloud loses 1 additional HP each round, even after stabilizing. The drain stops at 0 HP or higher. Protection from evil prevents it.

gm.title: Fog cadaver
lines:
Medium Undead, CR 1/2. 2d12 + 3 (16 HP), initiative −1, speed 20 ft. (4 squares). AC 10 (−1 Dex, +1 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 10. Base attack and grapple are unlisted. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +0, Ref −1, Will +3. Str 11, Dex 9, Wis 10, Cha 1. Toughness, +4 turn resistance, undead traits. Always neutral, no treasure. The printed mob is 9–73.
Attack or full attack. Slam +1 melee for 1d6. The cadaver can move or attack in a round, doing both only as part of a charge. Dreadful Moan (Ex) requires a DC 12 Fear save within 10 ft. Cadavers collapse if taken out of the fog or exposed to natural sunlight.

gm.title: Feeding and advancement
lines: If fewer creatures die in it during a week than its current HD, it loses 1 HD. If at least twice its HD die inside it during a week, it gains 1 HD.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: For the 6-HD fog, use the printed 60-ft. combat space and the description’s per-HD coverage for situational extent. A printed mob can exceed the sample fog’s 42-cadaver cap, so use current HP to determine how many the individual fog controls.
The cadaver’s moan gives a Fear save without a special failure effect or a repeat interval. Use the normal Ravenloft Fear result for the failed save.

gm.title: Description
lines: Azalin’s lumbering construct is stitched from several ruined zombies. Its smell reaches intruders well before its fists do.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative −1. AC 17 (−1 size, −1 Dex, +9 natural). Derived touch AC 8 and flat-footed AC 17. Base attack +12, grapple +16. Printed space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +6, Ref +5, Will +6.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +16 melee for 2d8 + 4 damage.
Standard Actions Only (Ex). Move or attack on a turn, or combine them as a charge. The chart separately lists a full attack of two slams at +16 for 2d8 + 4 each.
Stench (Ex). Coming within 30 ft. requires a DC 19 Fortitude save. Failure applies a −2 circumstance penalty to attacks, saves and skill checks for 1d6 + 4 minutes. Success grants immunity to this golem’s stench for one day.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Construct traits, damage reduction 10/magic. Magic Immunity (Ex) blocks spells, spell-like abilities and supernatural effects, with the listed exceptions. Targeted dispel magic with a check of at least 16 shuts it down for a number of rounds equal to the check result minus 10. A result of 26 or higher destroys it. Detect magic shows a growing magical aura while it is down. True resurrection destroys it immediately. Animate dead restores it to full HP.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land or underground. Solitary, always neutral, no treasure. Advancement 19–24 HD (Large) or 25–44 HD (Huge). A creator can command it within 60 ft. if it both sees and hears the creator. Otherwise it follows the last order and responds if attacked.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The source shows a two-slam full attack but separately restricts it to standard actions. Use a single slam unless another effect explicitly allows a full attack. Space and reach remain as printed despite the Large size.

gm.title: Description
lines: This decaying spellcaster directs other zombies from a distance and sees through their eyes. The sample is a 6th-level human adept with a toad familiar.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any land. Solitary. Usually neutral evil. Standard treasure. Advances by character class.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +2. AC +2 Dex, +4 natural, and +2 leather armor. Touch 12, flat-footed 16. Base attack +3, grapple +5. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +2, Ref +4, Will +8.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Concentration +7, Knowledge (arcana) +7, Knowledge (nature) +7, Listen +5, Profession (herbalist) +8, Spot +5, Search +3, Survival +12. Alertness, Brew Potion, Scribe Scroll, Toughness, Track.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Undead traits and toad familiar.
Aura of Death (Su). In the first round a living creature comes within 90 ft., it makes a DC 12 Fortitude save. Failure imposes a disease chosen by the zombie lord as contagion. A save failed by more than 10 kills the target and raises it as a zombie under the lord’s control. The lord cannot suppress the aura.
Speech of the Dead (Su). Speak telepathically with undead, which usually only report basic facts about their former lives and recent experiences. Use speak with dead at will by touching a corpse as a standard action.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +5 melee for 1d8 + 2. Full attack makes two such slams or a sling attack +5 ranged for 1d4.
Zombie Master (Su). Command zombies in sight mentally as a free action at will. The lord can see or otherwise sense through any zombie within a mile.
Awaken the Dead (Su). Use animate dead at caster level 12 to create zombies only.
Zombify (Su). On a successful touch attack against a living creature, a failed DC 12 Fortitude save kills the target. It rises after 1d4 rounds as a controlled zombie. Awaken the Dead and Zombify share one use per day.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines: Adept divine slots 4/3/2 for spell levels 0–2. Save DC 13 + spell level. The source leaves spell preparation to the DM.

gm.title: Adapting the encounter
lines: Apply to a humanoid or monstrous humanoid base. Its type becomes undead, Hit Dice become d12, and natural armor increases by +4. Keep speed, saves, skills, and base attacks. Add two slams if it had none. If armed, use the weapon as the primary attack and a slam as secondary. Slam base damage from Fine through Colossal: 1d2, 1d3, 1d4, 1d6, 1d8, 2d6, 2d8, 4d6, 4d8. Keep stronger original damage. Str +4, no Con. Add Toughness and increase CR by 3. Aura of Death and Zombify use DC 10 + half HD + Cha modifier.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed sample gives a single sling attack as the alternative to two slams. The general template allows a weapon attack with a secondary slam.
